episodes.title: The Empty Relief Fund
episodes.script:
SFX: Office doors slam against the wall. Wet boots strike marble. Papers scatter.
AGNES: I want the relief money opened now. Seventy settlers sailed. I have seventy names.
BELL: Madam, this is a private subscription office.
AGNES: It was public when you wanted our deposits.

SFX: Investors murmur. A chair scrapes back.

MILES: Uncle, is that one of the settlers?
AGNES: Agnes Murray. Seventeen pounds for thirty acres and three berths. Your clerk wrote it down himself.

SFX: A thick ledger lands on Bell’s desk.

AGNES: Read the names, Ewan.
EWAN: Agnes—
AGNES: Read them. You stood in Calderwick and watched us pay.

SFX: Pages turn slowly.

EWAN: Seventy deposits. Seventy passages.
AGNES: Then begin with the dead.

SFX: The room falls quiet.

AGNES: Three children buried above the tide line. A cooper dead of fever. Two infants without milk. Twelve people too weak to stand when I left. Thomas stayed because the others could not walk to the coast.
MARA: You left the settlement?
AGNES: There was no settlement. There was mud, jungle and paper money nobody would take.

SFX: A man in the investor crowd gives a shocked laugh.

INVESTOR: Paper money? Bell, you sold us a national bank.
BELL: The lady has endured a difficult voyage. We will not turn grief into accountancy.
AGNES: Accountancy put us on that ship.

SFX: Agnes tears pages from a small notebook and lays them down one by one.

AGNES: The families sold houses, workshops, carts and winter stock. Here are the amounts. Here are the children. Here are the graves.
MARA: Agnes, I did not know the ship lacked supplies.
AGNES: You knew I had children.
MARA: I believed there would be stores.
AGNES: Belief did not feed them.

SFX: Noon clock mechanism begins winding in the distance.

MACRAE: Mr Kerr, our relief treasury will answer this unfortunate spectacle.
EWAN: What relief treasury?
MACRAE: The Government Relief Fund of Ravenshore. You are its treasurer now.
EWAN: I have never seen that ledger.
MACRAE: Then this is an excellent morning to become familiar with your office.
AGNES: I do not want another title. I want food, medicine and passage home.
MACRAE: And you shall have figures prepared by noon.
EWAN: Figures are not money.
MACRAE: Mr Kerr, respectable men understand that the distinction is often temporary.

SFX: Investors whisper more loudly.

MILES: He cannot refuse, can he? His name is printed beneath Treasurer.
BELL: My nephew has identified the practical difficulty.

SFX: Bell slides a brass key across the desk.

BELL: Counting room, lower cabinet. Produce the relief balance before the clock strikes twelve. It would be regrettable if these investors concluded that their new treasurer could not locate his own fund.

SFX: A door opens. Fast footsteps descend stone stairs.

NARRATOR: Ewan had fifty-three minutes to find money in an office built to make paper resemble money.

SFX: Cabinet doors bang open. Ledgers thump onto a counting table.

PIPPA: Relief subscriptions, emigrant assistance, colonial stores. Three labels. All empty folders.
EWAN: Search cash transfers after the October auction.
PIPPA: Macrae’s account received the proceeds. Bell took commission. Ross took printing charges. The shipmaster took passage fees.
EWAN: There must be a reserve.
PIPPA: There is a column called reserve.
EWAN: Amount?
PIPPA: Blank.

SFX: Ewan rapidly turns pages.

EWAN: Here. “Emergency provision authorised against future land revenue.”
PIPPA: Authorised is not deposited.
EWAN: The investors were told two per cent went to settler relief.
PIPPA: Two per cent appears on every certificate.
EWAN: That is sixteen certificates’ worth from the first issue.
PIPPA: Yes.
EWAN: Where did it go?
PIPPA: Nowhere. It was printed as a benefit and never entered as cash.

SFX: The distant clock strikes the first warning quarter.

EWAN: Bell’s private daybook.
PIPPA: Locked.
EWAN: He gave me the cabinet key.
PIPPA: Not his desk key.
EWAN: Then bring the duplicate register.
PIPPA: Why?
EWAN: Every false account here borrows a number from a real one. If the relief fund exists only on paper, its number will belong to something else.

SFX: Two ledgers open side by side. Fingers track lines.

PIPPA: Fund R-F-nine.
EWAN: Freight account F-nine.
PIPPA: Same opening date.
EWAN: Same balance carried forward.
PIPPA: Four thousand eight hundred pounds.
EWAN: And the freight account closed when the expedition sailed.
PIPPA: They copied its balance into the relief ledger.
EWAN: Without transferring a penny.

SFX: A fist pounds on the counting-room door.

BELL: Twenty minutes, Mr Kerr.
EWAN: Open the door.

SFX: Lock turns. The investor chamber swells with impatient voices.

BELL: I trust you have found a reassuring answer.
EWAN: I found the figure used to advertise the relief fund.
MACRAE: Four thousand eight hundred pounds.
EWAN: That was the expedition freight balance. It was copied into a second ledger without a transfer.

SFX: Public murmurs sharpen.

INVESTOR: So the relief account was false?
BELL: Mr Kerr is describing an internal posting delay.
AGNES: Can you buy one sack of meal from it?
EWAN: No.
AGNES: One bottle of medicine?
EWAN: No.
AGNES: One berth home?
EWAN: No.

SFX: Agnes strikes the ledger with her palm.

AGNES: Then say it where they can hear you.
EWAN: The families were promised four thousand eight hundred pounds of emergency provision. No cash was deposited.

SFX: Several investors rise at once.

MILES: Uncle, you told us the settlers were protected.
BELL: Sit down, Miles.
MILES: Are they alive?
AGNES: Some were when I left.

SFX: Nothing. Long.

MACRAE: Mr Kerr, draft relief warrants against the next subscription issue.
EWAN: More bonds?
MACRAE: Assistance requires confidence. Confidence requires orderly sales.
AGNES: You would sell another family passage to rescue mine?
MACRAE: Mrs Murray, a sovereign administration cannot be governed by one distressed citizen.
AGNES: You have no administration. You have Ewan and a cupboard.

SFX: A few investors laugh. Macrae’s cane taps once.

MACRAE: Mr Kerr, your mother’s house is supported by wages from this office, is it not.
EWAN: Leave her outside this.
MACRAE: Of course. Have the warrants ready by noon tomorrow.

SFX: A messenger pushes through the crowd and places a sealed packet on the desk.

MESSENGER: Cross-Channel dispatch for the Ravenshore treasury. Immediate.
BELL: Give it to Mr Kerr. Apparently, he is the treasury.

SFX: Wax cracks. Paper unfolds.

PIPPA: There is no money in the relief ledger.
EWAN: But this sealed notice says a second ship of settlers is due to depart from France tomorrow morning.

episodes.title: The Complaint Book
episodes.script:
SFX: A government corridor echoes with running feet. A heavy registry book is dragged across a counter.
EWAN: Keep the book open. Seventy names must be entered before Bell closes this office.
CLERK: Complaints concerning foreign settlements require sworn evidence.
AGNES: I crossed an ocean to give it.

SFX: A door unlocks. Measured footsteps approach.

VEY: Nobody crosses my corridor at a run unless Parliament is burning.
EWAN: Sir, a second settler ship leaves France this morning.
VEY: Then speak without adjectives.
EWAN: The first expedition lacked office-supplied food, tools and medicine. Mrs Murray has returned from the advertised site. No capital was there. Seventy settlers were exposed, and another ship is being dispatched.
VEY: By whom?
EWAN: Lucien D’Arcy, acting through the Ravenshore treasury.
AGNES: Write down the people already lost.
VEY: This department does not certify deaths from a private colony.
AGNES: Then certify that I said their names in this building.

SFX: Agnes opens her notebook.

AGNES: Three children. One cooper. Two infants. Begin there.
CLERK: Sir?
VEY: Open the public complaint book.

SFX: A giant cover creaks. Pen scratches.

CLERK: Complainant?
AGNES: Agnes Murray. Settler. Mother. Former shopkeeper.
CLERK: Substance of complaint?
AGNES: We were sold a city. We found jungle and mud. We were sold stores. We found none. We were given Ravenshore notes. Nobody on the coast accepted them.
EWAN: Add the cargo reconciliation. Seventy passengers; no medical chest entered, no axes, no saws, no office food allocation.
VEY: Source?
EWAN: Bell’s freight ledger and Thomas Hale’s cargo list.
VEY: Your office title?

SFX: Ewan hesitates. Paper rustles in his hand.

EWAN: Treasurer of Ravenshore.
AGNES: They printed that yesterday. He did not hold the money when we sailed.
VEY: The qualification will be entered.

SFX: Pen scratches steadily.

CLERK: Complaint numbered forty-one. Supporting names appended: seventy.
AGNES: Read the entry aloud.
CLERK: “The losses and reported conditions of the first Ravenshore expedition are formally recorded pending inquiry.”

SFX: Agnes releases a shaking breath.

AGNES: Now they cannot say nobody told London.
VEY: Bell will sign an undertaking before you leave.

SFX: Another door opens. Bell enters, followed by Macrae and Miles.

BELL: Sir Alistair, an official summons before breakfast is rather theatrical.
VEY: So is a country without a recognized desk in any ministry.
MACRAE: Ravenshore’s standing does not depend upon London hospitality.
VEY: Its ships use European ports. Its bonds use London money. Today, that is sufficient hospitality.

SFX: A single sheet is placed on the desk.

VEY: Sign that no further settler expedition will depart until the first complaint is examined.
BELL: I do not command French shipping.
VEY: Your bank validates the treasury certificates.
BELL: Temporarily.
VEY: Your signature can also be temporary. Put it there.

SFX: Pen scratches.

BELL: There. No further expedition is authorised to leave.
VEY: Mr Kerr, take the duplicate.

SFX: Paper folds sharply.

EWAN: I am going to the French subscription sale.
MACRAE: You will return to the office.
EWAN: The sailing notice names Lucien. If his investors withdraw, his passengers cannot be financed.
MACRAE: Mr D’Arcy is conducting lawful treasury business.
AGNES: With families aboard?
MACRAE: Mrs Murray, your complaint has received the dignity of ink. Do not demand the indignity of influence.

SFX: Ewan turns and runs. Corridor doors slam behind him.

NARRATOR: The complaint was official by nine. At ten, Lucien’s sale opened three streets from Bell’s bank.

SFX: Auction bell rings. French and English voices bid over one another. Certificates flutter.

LUCIEN: Twelve acres with river frontage. Who offers twenty pounds?
EWAN: Stop the sale!

SFX: Bidding collapses into startled murmurs.

LUCIEN: Ah. Ravenshore sends its treasurer personally.
EWAN: No further expedition is authorised. Bell signed this undertaking less than an hour ago.
LUCIEN: I sell land, monsieur. Ships are a separate romance.
EWAN: Your notice says passengers depart this morning.
LUCIEN: Prospective passengers. Prospective mornings. Language must breathe.

SFX: Ewan lays the official undertaking on the auction table.

EWAN: Investors, the first expedition reached no capital. The office supplied no food, tools or medicine. The losses have been entered in a public complaint book.
INVESTOR: Is that Bell’s signature?
EWAN: Yes.
LUCIEN: And yours appears on the bonds, Treasurer.
EWAN: My initials were copied without permission.

SFX: Main doors open. Macrae’s cane crosses the floor, slow and distinct.

MACRAE: That is a serious defence from a man who has emptied his own treasury.
EWAN: What?
MACRAE: Mr D’Arcy, forgive this interruption. Our treasurer is distressed because an audit has discovered a shortage.
LUCIEN: How large?
MACRAE: Four thousand eight hundred pounds.

SFX: Investors react loudly.

MILES: That is the relief figure.
MACRAE: Precisely. Mr Kerr had sole responsibility for reconciling it yesterday.
EWAN: The account never held cash.
MACRAE: A convenient conclusion from the clerk controlling its ledger.

SFX: Bell arrives, breathing hard. A ledger lands on the auction table.

BELL: Ewan, I gave you an opportunity when others called you provincial and incompetent.
EWAN: You know that balance was copied from freight.
BELL: I know this ledger records a withdrawal under your authority.
EWAN: I made no withdrawal.
MACRAE: Then your seal has developed independence.

SFX: Pages turn. A metal seal knocks against wood.

LUCIEN: Investors, you are witnessing a treasury matter. The sale may continue at eleven.
INVESTOR: Not with a thief at the table.
SECOND INVESTOR: Search him.
EWAN: Nobody touches me.

SFX: Chairs scrape around Ewan.

BELL: There will be no vulgarity. Mr Kerr will answer one figure. Four thousand eight hundred pounds left the relief account. Where is it?
EWAN: It was never there.
MACRAE: His answer is now entered before witnesses.
MILES: Ewan, did you take it?
EWAN: No.
MACRAE: Then perhaps he intended to repay it after selling his mother’s property.
EWAN: Do not speak about her.
MACRAE: I merely read what your own security schedule provides.

SFX: Pippa pushes through the crowd and snatches the ledger.

PIPPA: This is not Ewan’s handwriting.
BELL: The seal is more authoritative than handwriting.
PIPPA: Let me see the withdrawal page.
MACRAE: Certainly. Accuracy has always been your office’s small consolation.

SFX: Pippa bends the page. Waxed paper crackles.

PIPPA: Ewan, look at the seal impression.
EWAN: The outer ring is mine. The centre has been recut.
BELL: An allegation made after discovery carries limited weight.
PIPPA: And this ink is still blue at the fold.
MACRAE: Enough.

SFX: Macrae pulls the ledger away. One loose schedule slips free and lands at Ewan’s feet.

EWAN: The theft ledger bears my forged seal.
PIPPA: And it lists your mother’s house as collateral for the missing funds.

episodes.title: The Newest Ink
episodes.script:
SFX: Auction-room doors are bolted. Ewan pounds on them from inside.
EWAN: Nobody leaves with that ledger. Pippa, give me the loose schedule.
MACRAE: Mr Kerr, an accused treasurer does not command the room.
PIPPA: He does if the accusation was printed yesterday.

SFX: Paper is smoothed across the auction table.

BELL: Choose your next words carefully, Miss Shaw. Your wages are not a shield.
PIPPA: No. The ink is.
LUCIEN: This sale has already lost an hour.
EWAN: Families may be boarding your ship now.
LUCIEN: Then your English dispute should become concise.

SFX: Pippa uncaps an ink bottle.

PIPPA: Bell’s old ledgers use iron-black ink. This withdrawal entry is blue-black.
BELL: Ink changes with storage.
PIPPA: Not into the exact colour on Ross’s newest certificates.
MACRAE: Similarity is not proof.
EWAN: Ross mixed the last batch himself. Send for him.
MACRAE: The printer is not accountable to a clerk.
BELL: The investors will not accept uncertainty over a treasury theft. Bring Ross.

SFX: Macrae’s cane stops tapping.

NARRATOR: For once, Bell’s fear of public doubt was useful to Ewan.

SFX: Bolts draw back. After a short rush of corridor noise, a printer’s case is set heavily on the table.

ROSS: I was told a certificate had failed.
PIPPA: Your ink did not.
ROSS: That sounds less like praise than usual.
EWAN: Examine the withdrawal entry, the security schedule and your newest Ravenshore certificate.

SFX: Glass stopper lifts. Paper edges rub. Ross sniffs the ink.

ROSS: Same blue-black.
MACRAE: Many printers use blue-black.
ROSS: Not this mixture. Two measures oak gall, one copper salt, gum reduced because the engraved borders smear.
PIPPA: When did you mix it?
ROSS: Three days ago.
EWAN: The ledger dates the withdrawal in October.

SFX: Investors erupt in angry voices.

INVESTOR: Then the entry is false!
MILES: Uncle, you said Ewan emptied the fund months ago.
BELL: Silence.
ROSS: There is more. This sheet carries powdered chalk from my drying rack. It has not been inside a ledger since October.
PIPPA: It was inserted recently.
ROSS: Yes.
MACRAE: You are a printer, Ross, not a magistrate.
ROSS: A magistrate may know law. I know what leaves my press.

SFX: Pippa places the loose schedule beside a new certificate.

PIPPA: The cut edges match.
EWAN: Same paper stock?
ROSS: Same mould lines. Same batch.
EWAN: Supplied for the issue naming me Treasurer.
ROSS: Yes.

SFX: Ewan turns pages quickly.

EWAN: The theft page was made from the newest bond paper, written in ink mixed three days ago, and inserted into an older relief ledger.
BELL: That does not identify who inserted it.
EWAN: No. It proves I did not authorize a withdrawal in October on paper that did not exist until this week.

SFX: Several palms strike the auction tables.

INVESTOR: Withdraw the accusation.
SECOND INVESTOR: And tell us where the money is.
MILES: Uncle, say it plainly.
BELL: My nephew will not direct this bank.
PIPPA: Then the figures will. Show us the cash account supporting the relief ledger.
BELL: That account is subject to reconciliation.
EWAN: I reconciled it yesterday. There was no deposit.
BELL: There were expected revenues.
EWAN: Expected from what?
BELL: Land subscriptions.
EWAN: Amount received?
BELL: The treasury operated across several accounts.
PIPPA: Name one holding cash.
BELL: Miss Shaw—
PIPPA: Name one.

SFX: Nothing. Long.

LUCIEN: Bell, my investors have been locked in a room while your clerks discuss ink. Give them a treasury balance.
BELL: Cross-Channel subscriptions are not yet posted.
LUCIEN: I sent the subscription total two days ago.
BELL: Less commissions, printing, passage and agency charges.
EWAN: Balance?
BELL: There are liabilities in transit.
MILES: Balance, Uncle.

SFX: Bell shuts the ledger.

BELL: The Ravenshore treasury presently holds no available cash.

SFX: A wave of voices crashes through the room.

INVESTOR: Empty?
SECOND INVESTOR: You sold us government bonds backed by an empty treasury!
MILES: You accused Ewan to hide that?
BELL: I relied upon documents submitted under sovereign authority.
MACRAE: Take care, Bell.
BELL: I am taking care. The planted withdrawal does not belong to my bank’s hand.
MACRAE: A courteous man does not abandon his partners because a clerk recognizes ink.
BELL: A sovereign man does not require his banker to forge a clerk’s seal.

SFX: Macrae’s cane strikes the table.

MACRAE: The seal was required because Mr Kerr refused the dignity of his appointment.
EWAN: You ordered it forged.
MACRAE: I ordered treasury documents completed.
PIPPA: With his mother’s house as collateral?
MACRAE: A treasurer must offer confidence.
EWAN: My mother never pledged her house.
BELL: Then the security schedule is invalid.
EWAN: Say the accusation was false.
BELL: The evidence against you was manufactured.
EWAN: In front of everyone.

SFX: Investors quieten.

BELL: Ewan Kerr did not withdraw four thousand eight hundred pounds from the Ravenshore relief account. The account contained no such money. The ledger entry accusing him was planted.

SFX: A single investor begins clapping. Others join, not in celebration but demand.

INVESTOR: Return our subscriptions.
BELL: The remaining certificates will be reviewed.
LUCIEN: Your review does not concern my completed sales.
EWAN: Your ship must be stopped.
LUCIEN: Bell signed an undertaking, not I.
BELL: My undertaking covers treasury authorization. No ship can lawfully depart under Ravenshore papers.
EWAN: Then send the port order now.
BELL: Miles, bring the dispatch book.

SFX: Miles opens a narrow book. Pages flick.

MILES: The cancellation order is not here.
BELL: I signed it at Vey’s office.
EWAN: You signed a promise. Did anyone send the order?
BELL: My secretary was instructed.
PIPPA: By whom?
BELL: By me.
PIPPA: There is no dispatch number.

SFX: Distant pounding at the outer doors.

MESSENGER: Open for a port telegram!

SFX: Bolts wrench back. A messenger runs in, paper shaking.

MESSENGER: Cross-Channel sailing confirmation for Mr D’Arcy.
LUCIEN: Give it here.
EWAN: Read it aloud.
LUCIEN: It is private commercial correspondence.
AGNES: There are families on that ship.

SFX: Agnes enters, boots hard on the floor, and tears the telegram from Lucien.

AGNES: Departure recorded at eight-ten this morning. Passengers and land purchasers aboard.
EWAN: How many?
AGNES: More settlers than the notice listed.
BELL: That cannot be correct. I signed that no further expedition would leave.
PIPPA: The port stamp is correct.
EWAN: When did it sail?
AGNES: The second ship already sailed from France this morning.
PIPPA: It left despite Bell’s signed promise that no further expedition would depart.

beat_sheet.what_happened: Agnes publicly presented the names and reported losses of the first expedition and demanded relief for the stranded settlers.

state_changes.fact: Agnes has made the first expedition's losses known inside Bell's office.
Mara learns that the first expedition lacked the promised settlement and supplies.
Bell faces public demands to account for settler relief.

beat_sheet.what_happened: Ewan and Pippa established that the stated relief balance of 4,800 pounds was copied from a freight account and was never deposited as cash.

state_changes.fact: The relief ledger is established as containing a copied balance but no money.
Ewan can prove that the advertised relief fund was unfunded.

beat_sheet.what_happened: Ewan publicly stated that no cash had been deposited into the relief fund, and a sealed notice revealed that a second settler ship was due to depart France the next morning.

state_changes.fact: Agnes learns that the relief fund cannot supply food, medicine, or return passage.
Ewan learns that a second settler expedition is imminent.
Its scheduled departure becomes known to Bell's office.

beat_sheet.location: Vey's government registry office in London
beat_sheet.what_happened: Vey ordered the first expedition's names and reported losses entered into a public complaint book and required Bell to sign that no further expedition would depart pending inquiry.

state_changes.fact: The first expedition's seventy names and reported losses are officially recorded.
Agnes obtains an official record of the settlers' complaint.
Bell signs an undertaking against further settler departures.

beat_sheet.what_happened: Ewan interrupted Lucien's sale with Bell's undertaking and warned investors that the first expedition's losses had been officially recorded.

state_changes.fact: Lucien's French-facing sale is disrupted by Ewan's warning.
Ewan publicly attempts to prevent financing and passage for the second expedition.

beat_sheet.what_happened: Macrae and Bell publicly accused Ewan of withdrawing 4,800 pounds from the relief treasury using a ledger entry bearing his seal.

state_changes.fact: Ewan is publicly accused of stealing the entire stated relief balance.
Bell relies on the theft ledger to shift responsibility for the empty treasury to Ewan.

beat_sheet.what_happened: Pippa and Ewan found that the theft ledger bore Ewan's forged seal and named Elspeth's house as collateral for the alleged missing funds.

state_changes.fact: Ewan learns that his forged authority has been used to place his mother's house at risk.
Elspeth's house is listed as collateral without her knowledge.
Pippa identifies physical signs that the theft entry was recently manufactured.

beat_sheet.what_happened: Ross confirmed that the theft entry used ink mixed three days earlier and paper from the newest bond issue, proving that it could not record an October withdrawal.

state_changes.fact: The alleged October withdrawal is proven to have been manufactured recently.
The documentary basis of the theft accusation against Ewan collapses publicly.
Macrae's planted evidence is exposed before investors.

beat_sheet.what_happened: Bell publicly admitted that the Ravenshore treasury held no available cash and that the ledger entry accusing Ewan had been planted.

state_changes.fact: Bell publicly admits that the treasury is empty and Ewan's alleged withdrawal was manufactured.
Ewan is publicly cleared of the 4,800-pound theft accusation.
The treasury is established as holding no available cash.

beat_sheet.what_happened: The second ship departed France at 08:10 carrying additional settlers despite Bell's signed undertaking against further departures.

state_changes.fact: The second settler ship has sailed from France.
Bell's signed undertaking fails to prevent the departure.

beat_sheet.note: The departure occurs away from the principal cast and remains open canon until the port confirmation reaches London.

beat_sheet.what_happened: A port confirmation revealed that the second ship had already sailed from France carrying more settlers despite Bell's signed promise.

state_changes.fact: Ewan learns that his attempt to stop the second expedition failed.
Agnes learns that additional settlers have been sent toward Ravenshore.
Bell is confronted with proof that a second expedition departed despite his undertaking.

promise_ledger.listener_is_waiting_for: whether the investor money transferred into Macrae's controlled account can be recovered
whether Thomas, Agnes, and the stranded settlers survive long enough to make London hear what happened
whether naming Ewan Treasurer of Ravenshore will make him legally responsible for the forged bond issue
whether Ewan can stop the second settler ship scheduled to leave France
promise_ledger.how_paid: A stamped port confirmation proves that the second ship sailed from France despite Bell's signed undertaking.

promise_ledger.listener_is_waiting_for: whether Ewan can prove that the theft ledger and collateral pledge against his mother's house were forged
promise_ledger.how_paid: Ross matches the ledger entry to ink mixed three days earlier and paper from the newest bond issue, forcing Bell to withdraw the theft accusation publicly.

promise_ledger.listener_is_waiting_for: whether the false collateral entry will cause Elspeth to lose her house
what happens to the settlers aboard the second ship that escaped Ewan's warning

dates_fixed.what: Bell's London investor salon and Ewan's discovery of the duplicate serial
Bell confines Ewan overnight while the auction shipment is dispatched
The Calderwick recruiting meeting takes final deposits
The seventy settlers' ship is scheduled to sail
The first public Ravenshore bond sale succeeds and the proceeds are transferred before delivery
The first expedition carrying seventy settlers departs
The first ship reaches the advertised site of the Ravenshore capital
Thomas's first letter reaches Bell's London office
Ewan reconciles the expedition and auction accounts before Bell's investors
Agnes confronts Bell's office and Ewan discovers the empty relief fund and the second expedition notice
The expedition complaint is publicly recorded and Ewan is accused of stealing the relief fund
The theft ledger is disproved, Bell admits the treasury is empty, and the second ship's departure is confirmed
The second settler ship departs France

periods_fixed.elapsed: the expedition departs the next day; its landing occurs sixty-seven days after the bond sale
one day between Thomas's letter reaching London and Ewan's public reconciliation
the second expedition is scheduled to depart the next morning
the ink examination and confirmation of the second ship's departure occur later the same day
